claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has severe lattice distortion due to its compositional complexity.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes thermally activated dislocation cross-slip.
Severe lattice distortion promotes more homogeneous and distributed dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced high-temperature dislocation activity gives WTaTiVZr greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Enhanced high-temperature dislocation activity gives WTaTiVZr greater toughness than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten exhibits more localized slip and lower ductility than WTaTiVZr under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The prepared equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a homogeneous initial microstructure.
The WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten specimens will have matched grain sizes and comparable baseline processing.

High-temperature deformation tests at approximately 1200 °C, combined with in-situ TEM, synchrotron diffraction, ex-situ TEM, and EBSD, can capture and quantify the relevant dislocation structures and activity.
The controlled comparison will subject WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten to equivalent loading, strain-rate, temperature, and atmospheric conditions.
Relative to pure tungsten, deformed WTaTiVZr will have a higher dislocation density.
Relative to pure tungsten, deformed WTaTiVZr will show more evidence of cross-slip.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will develop a more uniformly distributed dislocation network rather than localized slip bands.
The multicomponent nature of WTaTiVZr creates a rugged dislocation-energy landscape.
The rugged energy landscape facilitates thermally activated cross-slip and distributes dislocation motion throughout the WTaTiVZr microstructure.
The predicted dislocation-density, cross-slip, and deformation-homogeneity differences will correlate with greater tensile plastic strain and fracture toughness in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply near 1200 °C when thermally activated dislocation dynamics dominate.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or in different microstructural states.
Concurrent deformation mechanisms such as twinning could confound attribution of improved properties to dislocation cross-slip and distribution.
Failure to observe statistically greater dislocation density and cross-slip in WTaTiVZr, or failure to associate property improvements with dislocation behavior, would falsify the hypothesis.
